text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Technical wholesaler Reesink wants to slash 15 percent of its workforce. (p1)
- Dutch consumer price for coffee is expected to rise swiftly and sharply in very near future. (p1)
- Food and detergent group Unilever posts 11 pct higher first quarter net at 900 million guilders.(p1)
- Music and film group PolyGram is to do its own distribution of feature-length films in the U.S. (p3)
- Automation group LCI is to raise its subscribed share capital by nearly ten percent. (p3)
- Dutch PTT KPN continus to post losses on activities where it faces direct competition. (p3)
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT sees first quarter profit grow by two million guilders to 52 million. (p4)
- Chemicals concern DSM's pension fund PVM has sold its entire 200 million guilder stake in property fund Uni-Invest. (p15) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch Rail NS unit Infra Services goes to court over right to buy back the units NS is currently selling. (p2)
- Casino exploiter Holland Casino books 13 million guilders higher 1996 profit at 134.8 million. (p2)
- Junior finance minister Wim Vermeend's plans for new fiscal system meets with parliament's approval. (p3) DE TELEGRAAF
- PM Wim Kok may visit Britain's new PM Tony Blair this week. (p1)
- Customs and intelligence officers intercept ship with cocaine on its way from Curacao to the Netherlands. (p1)
- Waste disposal company AVR suffers from false competition through growing export of dangerous waste. (p6)
- De Boer Tents and its U.S. rival Academy in joint-venture to conquer the U.S. and South East Asia. (p13) TROUW
- Dutch railways NS seeks government's help to tackle noise pollution. (p3)
- Chairman of builders' association AVBB chairman an underground rail link between Amsterdam, The Hague, Rotterdam and Utrecht. (p3) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Standard & Poor lowers Dutch PTT KPN's rating from neutral to negative. (p11)
- Loss to output through lack of telephone contact in the Netherlands up 30 percent to 838 million guilders in 1996. (p11)
